trend_analysis.methodological_note: The OLS slope is an empirical descriptive summary of the observed historical trend, not proof of a deterministic data-generating process.

seasonality_evidence.interpretation_notes: The observed lag-52 autocorrelation is r_52 = 0.4964 with 95% CI [0.1793, 0.8136], which exceeds the white-noise null threshold (+/-0.1356). This provides empirical evidence of annual cyclicality. Higher weekly volumes are observed in Q4 (Sep-Dec), but causal drivers cannot be asserted from transactional totals alone.

adf_test.hypothesis: H0: Unit root present (non-stationary); H1: Stationary/trend-stationary

kpss_level_test.hypothesis: H0: Series is level-stationary around a constant; H1: Non-stationary / unit root / trending

kpss_trend_test.hypothesis: H0: Series is trend-stationary around a deterministic linear trend; H1: Non-stationary / unit root

stationarity_tests.joint_diagnostic_assessment: Evidence is consistent with an observed upward trend, but stationarity diagnostics require consideration of deterministic trend and seasonality. Specifically: 1. The ADF test rejects the unit-root null (p = 0.0008). 2. The KPSS level test (c) rejects level-stationarity (p <= 0.01), indicating the mean is not constant over time. 3. The KPSS trend test (ct) fails to reject trend-stationarity (statistic 0.0875 vs 5% critical value 0.146, p >= 0.10). Limitations: These standard tests do not formally model the observed 52-week seasonal amplitude changes or evolving volatility. Therefore, forecasting models should explicitly account for trend and annual seasonality (e.g. via seasonal differencing, structural decomposition, or seasonal time-series models) rather than assuming unconditional stationarity.

key_findings: The weekly demand exhibits an observed upward trend with an empirical OLS slope of +0.86 units/week.
Annual expansion: Annual weekly mean grew from 146.9 units/week in 2014 to 238.8 units/week in 2017 (+62.6% total expansion across complete years).

Autocorrelation & cyclical evidence: Autocorrelation at lag 1 is r_1 = 0.6974 (95% CI [0.5618, 0.833]) and lag 52 is r_52 = 0.4964 (95% CI [0.1793, 0.8136]), both exceeding the white-noise null threshold (+/-0.1356).
Seasonal concentration: 11 of the 12 unusually high demand weeks (> 386.1 units) occurred in the September–December window.

Stationarity diagnosis: ADF rejects unit root (p = 0.0008) while KPSS level rejects constant mean (p <= 0.01) and KPSS trend fails to reject trend-stationarity (p >= 0.10). Stationarity diagnostics require consideration of deterministic trend and seasonality.
